metadata.issueBody:
# Update strip line does not say a hook refusal can clear

Leftover of #4845 after critic 5769478889, successor lean 5769543828, and Handoff 5769547277. Operator confirmed filing on 2026-09-21. The empty-object write stays. Do not ingest #4845 as "stop writing {}".

## Summary

When a host is already opted out and the hook file has no unrelated keys, `deft update` rewrites that tracked file to `{}`. That write is the leftover-free host-disable strip. An agent blocked by a hook refusal can run `deft update`, see the refusal clear, and commit the emptied file as the fix.

The update line already says the hooks were removed for an opt-out. It does not say a refusal can clear because the gate left. The disable disclosure has the same gap.

## Bound remedy

1. Keep the leftover-free `{}` write when the host is already disabled and the file has no unrelated keys.
2. Add one sentence on the existing update strip line and on the disable disclosure: a hook refusal can clear because the gate was removed.

## Measured (dispatch-sha 549e639a525e013616c7582b3825584d15f20f09)

- `packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts` strips a host only when that host is disabled and the file already exists. A Directive-only file becomes `{}`. The test "writes leftover-free opted-out Directive-only deposits as empty objects" expects `{}\n` for `.claude/settings.json` and `.grok/hooks/deft.json`.
- Update prints `Removed Directive-managed agent hooks (plan.policy.hostHooks opt-out): ...` and `stripped: ...`. Neither sentence says a hook refusal can start succeeding because the gate left.
- `HOST_HOOKS_DISABLE_CAPABILITY_COST_DISCLOSURE` in `packages/core/src/policy/host-hooks.ts` says opted-out hosts lose deft-hook guardrails and leftover-free files write `{}`. It does not say a refusal in the current session can clear because those commands were removed.

## Out of scope

Do not stop the `{}` write. Do not leave the commands in the tracked file. Do not replace `{}` with a marker object. Those were the refuted part of #4845.
